title: How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary with Remote Area Housing Salary Sacrifice
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week, including casual loading, super, and the impact of remote area housing salary sacrifice on your take-
salarySummary: Your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by your weekly hours and 52 weeks, assuming a standard 38-hour week for full-time work.

faqs.q: What is the formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice arrangements.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of your base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you are a casual employee, you add 25% to your base rate before calculating annual pay. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. Super is then paid on the ordinary earnings, which includes the loading.

faqs.q: What is remote area housing salary sacrifice and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Remote area housing salary sacrifice allows you to use pre-tax income to pay for housing costs if you live and work in a designated remote area. This reduces your taxable income, meaning you pay less tax and Medicare levy. It does not change your gross annual salary calculation, but it increases your take-home pay. The Australian Taxation Office sets the rules for this arrangement.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

To work out your annual salary from an hourly rate, use the simple formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work a different pattern, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30 and you work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This is the figure before tax, the Medicare levy, and any salary sacrifice arrangements. It also does not include superannuation, which is paid on top.

You can also think in terms of a fortnight. Multiply your weekly pay by two to get your gross fortnightly amount. For the example above, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280. This can help when comparing with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate usually includes a 25% casual loading. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. When using [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. Do not type a rate that already includes the loading; the calculator applies it correctly.

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a permanent employee. With casual loading, that becomes $33.05 per hour. Many award rates are higher than the minimum, so check your specific award through [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (the super guarantee). For a full-time employee earning $59,280, the employer contributes an additional $7,113.60 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer. This means your total remuneration package is higher than your gross salary.

## Remote Area Housing Salary Sacrifice

If you live and work in a remote area, you may be able to use a remote area housing salary sacrifice arrangement. This allows you to direct part of your pre-tax salary towards housing costs, such as rent or mortgage payments. The Australian Taxation Office sets the rules for what qualifies as a remote area. By reducing your taxable income, you pay less income tax and Medicare levy, increasing your take-home pay.

For example, if your gross annual salary is $80,000 and you sacrifice $10,000 for remote area housing, your taxable income becomes $70,000. You then pay tax on the lower amount, saving you money. This arrangement does not change the gross annual figure calculated from your hourly rate, but it affects the net amount you receive. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% on income above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, with reductions available for low-income earners. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed.

Salary sacrifice, such as remote area housing, reduces your taxable income, so you pay less tax and Medicare. However, this estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or other deductions. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a more detailed estimate.

## Award Rates and Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor, but most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. Award rates vary by industry and classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) information and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) details. If you are covered by an award, use that rate rather than the minimum. The figures in this article are averages or minimums, not a median for any specific job.

## Using the Timesheet

To convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly pay, visit [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate, select your weekly hours, and check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator shows gross pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember that super is paid on top and is not deducted from your pay. The results are estimates only.

For more information on average earnings, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, while all employees total earnings averaged $1,579.20 per week (including part-time workers). These are averages, not medians for a particular job.

This article provides a general guide. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary packaging. Always check your pay slip and consult a professional for personalised advice.
